title: std::map
learningGoals: read and write with square brackets
loop over a map in sorted order

youtube.title: C++ std::map: Key and Value | C++ Programming EP 72
youtube.description: In this episode you will store key and value pairs, read and write with square brackets and loop over a map in sorted order, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 std::map · 0:51 A phone book · 1:31 Sorted by key · 2:01 Second program · 3:01 Recap · 3:31 Bug of the Day · 4:19 Challenge · 4:39 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "STD::MAP" in tomato on lilac; Xecxec next to a phone book with names and numbers; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a phone book with names and numbers

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we look things up by name. A map stores keys and values, and keeps the keys in sorted order.

scenes.onScreen: "std::map": numbered lines (1. A map stores key and value pairs; 2. Keys are unique and sorted; 3. Square brackets create a missing key) and an analogy card: a phone book: look up a name, and get a number
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A map stores pairs. Each pair has a key and a value. Keys are unique, and the map keeps them sorted. You use the key to find the value. Square brackets read a value. But beware. If the key is missing, square brackets create it. Think of a phone book. You look up a name, and you get a number.
points: A map stores key and value pairs
Square brackets create a missing key

analogy.title: std::map
analogy.body: A phone book: look up a name, and get a number

scenes.onScreen: phone.cpp: a map from names to numbers
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 7] The map has string keys and int values. [HL 8] Square brackets with a key store a value. [HL 9] A second key is added. [HL 10] Using the same key again replaces the value. [HL 11] Asha now has ninety-five. [HL 12] The size is two, because keys are unique.

scenes.onScreen: a table: the map content in key order
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The map keeps the keys in sorted order. Asha comes before Ravi. Each key appears once. The value of Asha was replaced, so the old ninety-one is gone.

diagram.caption: a table: the map content in key order

scenes.onScreen: walk.cpp: a range-based for gives each key and value
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 7] We start the map with a list of pairs. [HL 8] The loop unpacks each pair into a name and marks. The order is sorted by key. Asha, Meera, then Ravi. [HL 11] Find looks up a key without creating it. [HL 12] If it equals end, the key is missing. [HL 13] Otherwise, second is the value.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as walk dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Asha, Meera and Ravi with their marks, and then Found eighty-eight.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A map stores key and value pairs. Two. Keys are unique and sorted. Three. Square brackets read or create a key. Four. Find looks up a key without creating it. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A map stores key and value pairs.
Square brackets read or create a key.
Find looks up a key without creating it.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A lookup that creates a key
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We only wanted to check for Ravi. But the size is two, not one. Square brackets created the key Ravi, with the value zero. Use count or find to check without changing the map.

scenes.onScreen: My map was lost. It had all the keys, but no values.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: My map was lost. It had all the keys, but no values.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Make a map from names to marks. Add three students. Print the one with the highest marks. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: unordered map. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

No Ravi
2
bug.why: Square brackets create a missing key with a default value. So a simple look-up grows the map. Use find or count to check.

pun: "My map was lost. It had all the keys, but no values."
challenge: Make a map from names to marks. Add three students. Print the one with the highest marks.
challengeAnswer: Loop over the map. Keep the best name and best marks. If a student has more marks than the best, replace both.
